headline: Hanceville council tables vehicle policy, passes credit card rules and moves its Thanksgiving meeting to Nov. 24
summary: At its Oct. 22 meeting the council put the take home vehicle policy on hold for six months, approved a city credit card policy and a $50,500 Public Works tractor, and set holiday dates for Veterans Park.
body: The Hanceville City Council worked through a full agenda on Thursday, Oct. 22, and the biggest change for residents is on the calendar. The meeting that would have fallen on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, now moves to Tuesday, Nov. 24. The next regular meeting is Thursday, Nov. 12, at City Hall, 112 Main Street SE.

The proposed vehicle policy, Resolution 2026-8, is on hold for six months. It would limit which city employees can take city vehicles home after their shift, and Public Works employees pushed back on it earlier this month. The vote to postpone passed with Councilman Robert Powell voting no. Mayor Nolan Bradford said the council will keep working on the policy with Public Works Director Rusty Fields during that time.

Three ordinances that would have given the council, instead of the mayor, the power to appoint the fire chief, Public Works director and parks director did not move forward. Each got a motion from Powell but no second. A related resolution on the interview process for those jobs was postponed so it can be rewritten.

The council did approve Resolution 2026-9, a policy for city issued credit cards, and a $50,500 tractor for Public Works from Frederick's Outdoors in Decatur after a $4,000 municipal discount. It also opted in to Alabama's Severe Weather Preparedness Sales Tax Holiday, so qualifying storm supplies will be free of city sales tax during the state's holiday in February 2027.

Holiday plans are taking shape too. Setup for the Tinsel Trail at Veterans Park starts Nov. 14, and the Christmas Tree Lighting is planned for Nov. 21. The Cullman County Christmas Parade is set for Dec. 5, with closures expected on Michelle Street and Park Street. The council also reappointed Margie Burkhart, Delton Blalock, Garrett Gilliland and Robert Powell to three year terms on the Historic Preservation Commission.
Find upcoming meeting dates with Add to calendar buttons on our City Council page, and read the official agendas on the City of Hanceville website.

headline: Signed minutes from the Oct. 8 council meeting show new park addresses, a $30 Holly Market vendor fee and a pool leak
summary: The city posted the official minutes from the Oct. 8 Hanceville City Council meeting. They list new addresses planned for C.W. Day Park and the pool, a $30 fee for Holly Market vendors, and a pool leak crews still have not found.
body: The City of Hanceville has posted the official minutes from the Oct. 8 City Council meeting. Mayor Nolan Bradford and City Clerk Teja McIntyre signed them on Oct. 26. The biggest votes from that night, including $25,000 more for road paving and the vote to uphold the removal of Fire Chief Chris Hardin, were covered in our earlier story. The minutes add a few details residents may want to know.

C.W. Day Park is getting a new address. The minutes say the park and a funeral home currently share the same address, so the park will become 100 Park Rd. and the pool will become 200 Park Rd. The minutes do not give a date for the change, so keep using the current address for now.
Vendors in the Hanceville Holly Market will pay only a $30 fee, according to the council's discussion. The indoor holiday market is set for the Hanceville Civic Center on Saturdays in December.

The park director told the council the leak in the city pool still has not been found, and the pool keeps losing water and chemicals. Cooler weather should cut chemical use a lot. Asbestos has been removed from the Park House, security cameras have been ordered, and bills for the fence project have started to come in.

The Fire Department reported 116 calls for the month and 1,106 so far this year. Two firefighters are in firefighter survival training, and Assistant Fire Chief Absher was set to take a traffic incident management trainer class in Cullman on Oct. 13 and 14.

The council also named Mayor Bradford, Mayor Pro Tem Jana Shelton, Councilor Kim Brown and Josh Howell to the Policy and Procedures Committee working to bring back a city police department. Councilor Robert Powell suggested looking at Sprout as the city's internet provider. Votes on the credit card policy and several ordinances were pushed to later meetings, and the council took up most of them on Oct. 22.
The next regular council meeting is Thursday, Nov. 12, at City Hall, 112 Main Street SE. You can read the full minutes on the city's website.

headline: Good Hope's planned hotel waits on a gas line under I-65 as a new package store gets ready to open
summary: Mayor Jerry Bartlett says a hotel planned off County Road 490 is on hold until natural gas can cross the interstate, while a new package store across from the Scotty Hooper Museum nears its opening.
body: A hotel is in the works for Good Hope, but it can't move forward until the city gets natural gas service under Interstate 65, Mayor Jerry Bartlett said after the Good Hope City Council's regular meeting on Monday, Oct. 26, according to The Cullman Tribune.

The city first asked to run its gas line through a crossing being built under the interstate for water lines, but was told the opening was too small. Grant money is now paying to upsize that water line because the area needs more water capacity, and city leaders hope the larger casing will leave room for Good Hope's gas line too.

City officials are scheduled to meet with Cullman County leaders about the project on Thursday, Nov. 5. No firm timeline has been set. Bartlett said a hotel would give visitors a place to stay overnight and keep them, and their spending, in Good Hope and Cullman County longer.

In the meantime, a new package store owned by Donald Estess, with his sons Scotty and Skipper also part of the business, is getting ready to open in a new building at 6073 County Road 490, Suite A, across from the Scotty Hooper Museum. The hotel is planned behind that store. A ribbon cutting is expected soon, but a date had not been set as of the Tribune's report.

headline: A $50,000 Lowe's grant will turn the Cullman County Public Library's back lawn into a play area and outdoor reading space
summary: The main library on Clark Street is one of 100 nonprofits nationwide picked for a 2026 Lowe's Community Impact Grant, and it hopes to break ground within a couple of weeks.
body: The grassy lot behind the Cullman County Public Library's main branch at 200 Clark St. NE is about to become a place to play and read. The library received a $50,000 Lowe's Community Impact Grant to build a play area and quiet outdoor reading spaces there, The Cullman Tribune reported on Oct. 27.

The library is one of only 100 nonprofits across the country chosen for the grant this year. Lowe's describes the project as a playground and rock garden meant to give children a safe place to play, families a place to gather and readers a peaceful spot outdoors.

Assistant Director Shelby Creekmore told the Tribune the library hopes to break ground within the next couple of weeks. Yearwood Construction is working on the project, a design rendering will be shared once it is final, and a grand opening date will be announced later.

The outdoor space is one piece of a larger plan. The library is working with Williams Blackstock Architects on future renovations and additions to the building, which has served the county since 1967. You can follow the library's plans at cullmanlib.org.

headline: Cold Springs sweeps cross country sectionals as five county teams head to state, and Hanceville's runners finish the season
summary: Cold Springs, both Cullman squads and the Holly Pond girls earned team berths for the Nov. 7 state meet in Moulton, while the Hanceville boys placed ninth in Class 3A Section 3.
body: Cold Springs won both the girls and boys titles at the Class 1A-2A Section 3 cross country meet on Thursday, Oct. 29, leading a strong day for Cullman County runners, The Cullman Tribune reported.

Cullman's boys placed second and its girls third in Class 5A Section 5, and the Holly Pond girls took the fourth and final team berth in Class 3A Section 3. Those five teams will be joined by 15 individual qualifiers from Vinemont, Holly Pond, Good Hope, West Point, Fairview, Cullman Christian and St. Bernard at the AHSAA State Cross Country Championships on Saturday, Nov. 7, at Oakville Indian Mounds Park in Moulton.

In Class 3A Section 3 at Munford, the Hanceville boys placed ninth with 268 points, led by Ely Stinson in 51st place. Two Hanceville girls also ran, though the Lady Bulldogs did not post a team score. No Hanceville runners advanced to state this year.
Congratulations to every local runner on a great season, and good luck to the county's state qualifiers in Moulton.

headline: Dry skies for Friday night trunk or treats, but showers are likely on Halloween night
summary: The National Weather Service calls for a mostly cloudy, mild Friday night, then a 30 percent chance of showers Saturday afternoon that climbs to 60 percent after dark on Halloween.
body: Good news for tonight's trunk or treats: the National Weather Service forecast for Hanceville calls for a mostly sunny Friday with a high near 79, then a mostly cloudy night with a low around 57 and only a light breeze.

Halloween itself looks less certain. Saturday should be mostly cloudy with a high near 75, and showers become possible after 3 PM, with about a 30 percent chance. East winds of 5 to 10 mph could gust to 20 mph. Rainfall during the day should stay under a tenth of an inch.

Saturday night is the wetter part of the weekend. The forecast gives showers a 60 percent chance after dark, with a low around 55 and gusts up to 25 mph. Rain stays likely on Sunday, at about 70 percent, with a cooler high near 66.

If your family has plans Saturday, like the Drive Through Trick or Treat at Hanceville Fire Station #1 from 4 PM to 8 PM, the Berlin trunk or treat or Nightmare on Woodland Street in Cullman, pack rain jackets and check the host's page before you head out in case times change. No weather alerts were active for Hanceville as of Friday morning. Forecasts change, so check weather.gov for the latest.

headline: Cullman County Public Library opens a November short story challenge for writers of every age
summary: Writers of all ages can enter a story of 1,000 to 5,000 words from Nov. 2 through Nov. 25, and the library hosts a free writing workshop on Nov. 4.
body: Got a story in you? The Cullman County Public Library wants to read it. In honor of National Novel Writing Month, the library is holding a short story writing challenge from Monday, Nov. 2, through Wednesday, Nov. 25.

Entries should run between 1,000 and 5,000 words. The contest is open to every age, with stories judged in two groups: adults 18 and older, and kids 17 and under. Writing prompts and submission sheets are waiting at the library for anyone who needs a starting point.
Need a push to get going? The library will host a writing workshop for adults and students in grade 5 and up on Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 4:00 PM.

Pick up prompts and contest details at the main library, 200 Clark Street NE in Cullman, call 256-734-2720, or visit cullmanlib.org. Library hours are 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Monday through Friday and 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM on Saturday.

headline: West Point volleyball reaches the state semifinals as Addison wins its 16th state title
summary: West Point and Cold Springs closed their seasons at the state tournament in Birmingham, and neighboring Addison beat Meek for a second straight Class 1A championship.
body: Two Cullman County volleyball teams wrapped up their seasons this week at the AHSAA state tournament at Bill Harris Arena in Birmingham, and a nearby rival brought home another state championship.

West Point opened Class 4A play on Wednesday, Oct. 28, with a 3 to 0 sweep of Satsuma. The Warriors met defending champion Guntersville in the semifinals that afternoon and fell 25 to 13, 25 to 17 and 25 to 22. Guntersville went on to beat Orange Beach on Thursday for its second straight Class 4A title.

Cold Springs earned its trip to Birmingham with a five set win over Pisgah at the North Super Regional in Hoover. The Eagles drew No. 5 Ariton in the Class 2A quarterfinals on Oct. 28 and lost 3 to 0.

In Class 1A, Addison beat Winston County rival Meek 3 to 1 on Oct. 28, winning 25 to 11, 21 to 25, 25 to 23 and 26 to 24. It is the Bulldogs' second straight state championship and the 16th in program history. Ava Bartlett was named tournament MVP with 21 kills, three aces and eight digs, and Addison finished the season 34 and 12.
Congratulations to every player, coach and family who made the trip. Check our homepage for more local scores and Friday night football updates.

headline: About 1,600 eighth graders try out careers at Wallace State's Tools of the Trade
summary: Students from Cullman, Blount and Winston counties spent Tuesday on the Hanceville campus trying hands on stations in health care, manufacturing, skilled trades and more.
body: Wallace State Community College's Hanceville campus was packed with eighth graders on Tuesday, Oct. 27, for the college's yearly Tools of the Trade career showcase. About 1,600 students from Cullman, Blount and Winston counties came to get an early look at jobs they could train for close to home.

Students moved through interactive stations covering advanced manufacturing, health care, skilled trades, public safety, information technology and other high demand fields. They talked with local businesses and industries along with Wallace State's academic, health and technical programs.

The timing is on purpose. The showcase reaches students right before high school, when they start choosing classes and career pathways. Wallace State presents the event with the Cullman Area Chamber of Commerce, the City of Cullman Economic Development Agency, the Blount County Economic Development Agency and Cullman County Economic Development.
Learn more about Wallace State's career and workforce programs at wallacestate.edu, or visit our Wallace State page for campus links and upcoming events.

headline: Mud Creek Arts and Crafts Festival returns to downtown Hanceville Nov. 7
summary: The free street festival marks its 16th year on Commercial Street from 9 AM to 4 PM, and vendor booths and sponsorships are still open.
body: Mark Saturday, Nov. 7, on the calendar. The 16th annual Mud Creek Arts and Crafts Festival will fill historic downtown Hanceville from 9 AM to 4 PM along Commercial Street, centered at 106 Commercial St. NE. Admission is free, and the festival goes on rain or shine.

Friends of the Festival organizes the day. Expect street vendors with handmade goods, food trucks and local eateries, plus bounce houses and other activities for kids. Past years have brought woodwork, jewelry, seasonal decor, cutting boards, 3D printed pieces and homemade foods, so it is a good chance to get an early start on holiday shopping.

Downtown merchants usually keep their doors open during the festival, which makes it an easy day to stroll Commercial Street and visit Hanceville's shops and restaurants. The festival began as a way to bring more attention to the city's historic downtown, and it has grown into one of Hanceville's signature fall traditions.

Local artists, crafters and businesses can still sign up. A 10 by 10 foot vendor booth costs $40, and vendors are asked to stay for the whole event unless they sell out. Sponsorships range from $50 to $1,000 and must be received by Sunday, Nov. 1, to appear on the sponsorship banner. Silver sponsorships and above include free exhibit space.

Applications and payment can be mailed to Friends of the Festival, P.O. Box 600, Hanceville, AL 35077. Follow the festival's Facebook Page for updates, and find the date on our Events page with directions and an Add to calendar button.

headline: Wallace State sets a new fall enrollment record with 7,141 students
summary: Hanceville's community college topped 7,100 students for the first time in its history, its fourth straight fall increase. Spring 2027 registration is open now.
body: More students than ever are walking the Wallace State campus this fall. The college reports 7,141 students enrolled for the Fall 2026 semester as of Wednesday, Oct. 21, the first time it has passed 7,100.

That is 155 more students than last fall, when enrollment stood at 6,986. It is also the fourth fall in a row that enrollment has gone up. Since Fall 2022, when the college counted 5,966 students, enrollment has grown by nearly 20 percent.

Wallace State President Dr. Vicki P. Karolewics tied the record to the college's recognition as an Aspen Prize finalist, saying it reflects the work done across campus to help students start early, start right, finish and succeed.

Thinking about classes? Registration for Spring 2027 is open now. Regular term and Mini Term I classes start Jan. 8, and Mini Term II starts March 8. Lion Central can help at 256.352.8236, or visit wallacestate.edu.

headline: About 500 seniors filled the fairgrounds for Senior Day at the Cullman County Fair
summary: The Cullman County Commission on Aging says roughly 500 people 55 and older came out Wednesday for free admission, a free lunch, live music and a moment honoring veterans.
body: Wednesday was a big day for Cullman County's seniors. About 500 people age 55 and older spent Oct. 21 at the Cullman County Fairgrounds for Senior Day at the Cullman County Fair, according to Commission on Aging Director Stephanie Lawson.

Admission, parking and lunch were all free. Lawson thanked the Lions Club for cooking extra corn dogs and hot dogs for the large crowd, and Jamie Looney and her Grand Ole Opry group provided the entertainment. Aveanna sponsored the event and Premier Bank sponsored the lunch. There were no rides for the group, but guests toured the exhibits and picked up candied apples.
One of the highlights was a tribute to veterans, who were called up and given certificates while a patriotic song played. Lawson said everyone was on their feet to thank them.

Several elected officials spoke as well. Lawson noted it was the final Fair Day stage appearance in their current roles for Sheriff Matt Gentry, Revenue Commissioner Barry Willingham and Commissioner Garry Marchman.
Looking for activities for seniors in Hanceville and around the county? The Commission on Aging posts its programs at co.cullman.al.us/coa and on its Facebook Page.

headline: Cold Springs and West Point volleyball head to the state tournament next week
summary: Both Cullman County teams won five set third place matches at the North Super Regional in Hoover and will play in the state quarterfinals at the Birmingham CrossPlex on Wednesday, Oct. 28. For Cold Springs, it is the first state trip since 1989.
body: Two Cullman County volleyball teams are still playing in late October. Cold Springs and West Point both earned spots in next week's AHSAA state tournament at the North Super Regional in Hoover.

West Point beat Sylacauga in five sets on Thursday to clinch its state berth. The Warriors fell to top ranked Guntersville in Friday's Class 4A semifinal, then came back to beat Moody in five sets, winning the deciding set 15 to 12. That third place finish makes West Point the North's No. 3 seed. The Warriors are 39 and 10.

Cold Springs swept J.B. Pennington on Thursday to clinch its berth. The Eagles lost to top ranked Fyffe in Friday's Class 2A semifinal, then outlasted Pisgah in five sets, taking the final set 16 to 14, to claim the North's No. 3 seed. According to The Cullman Tribune, this will be Cold Springs' first state tournament appearance since 1989.

West Point opens the Class 4A state tournament against South No. 2 seed Satsuma at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday, Oct. 28. Cold Springs faces South No. 2 seed Ariton at 1:30 p.m. the same day. State tournament matches are at the Birmingham CrossPlex.
Good luck to both teams from all of us in Hanceville.

headline: Friday night roundup: Addison wins region title, Vinemont clinches seventh straight playoff trip
summary: Addison finished a perfect 10 and 0 regular season with a Class 1A, Region 7 title, Vinemont rallied late to make the playoffs again, and Cold Springs, Cullman and Good Hope all won big on the last region night of the season.
body: It was a big Friday night across Cullman County as region play wrapped up and playoff spots were settled.

Addison beat previously unbeaten Hackleburg 33 to 7 at home, scoring 33 straight points and picking off four passes. The Bulldogs finished the regular season 10 and 0, went 7 and 0 in Class 1A, Region 7, and earned the region's No. 1 playoff seed.

Vinemont won 12 to 7 over Susan Moore on senior night. Josh Rhodes hit Travis Speer for a 19 yard touchdown on fourth down with 4:17 left, sending the Eagles to their seventh playoff appearance in a row. Vinemont finished the regular season 6 and 4, and 4 and 3 in Class 3A, Region 6.

Cold Springs won 56 to 6 at Carbon Hill to improve to 8 and 1, its third straight win. Cullman pulled away for a 42 to 13 win at Jackson Olin in Class 5A, Region 5 play, and Good Hope scored 42 straight points to beat Hayden 42 to 7 on senior night, moving to 7 and 2 overall and 6 and 1 in Class 4A, Region 8.

It was a tougher night for a few county teams. Etowah beat Holly Pond 43 to 12, dropping the Broncos to 2 and 7. Deshler beat West Point 55 to 14 in the Warriors' season finale, and Oneonta shut out Hanceville 62 to 0 at Ray Talley Stadium.
Hanceville closes its season Friday, Oct. 30, at Elkmont. Follow that game in our Game Center.

headline: Oneonta beats Hanceville 62 to 0; Bulldogs close the season at Elkmont next Friday
summary: The Bulldogs fell to 8 and 1 Oneonta in their final home game of the year Friday night at Ray Talley Stadium. Hanceville wraps up the regular season Oct. 30 at Elkmont.
body: Friday night at Ray Talley Stadium was a tough one for the Hanceville Bulldogs. Oneonta, one of the strongest teams in Class 3A, Region 6, won 62 to 0 in what AL.com called an early final in its statewide Week 10 coverage.

The loss drops Hanceville to 0 and 9 overall and 0 and 7 in region play. Oneonta scored 35 points in the first quarter, led 56 to 0 at halftime and finished its region schedule unbeaten at 7 and 0, improving to 9 and 1, according to The Cullman Tribune.
It was the last home game of the season, so thank you to the players, coaches, band, cheerleaders and every fan who came out to support the Bulldogs at home this fall.
The Bulldogs close the regular season on the road at Elkmont on Friday, Oct. 30, at 7 p.m. Follow the score in our Game Center.

headline: Country Wok adds ramen, Hong Kong wontons and a matcha cannoli to its downtown Hanceville menu
summary: Owner Kenny Lee keeps the menu small and the ingredients local, and he just added four new dishes at 107 Bangor Ave. Open Tuesday through Saturday, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.
body: Hanceville's go to Chinese spot has something new to try. Country Wok, owned and run by Kenny Lee, has added four dishes to its menu.

The new items are ramen, Japanese hot dogs, Hong Kong wontons and a matcha cannoli. The ramen and wontons sit nicely beside the Korean wings, the Japanese hot dog makes a fun street food pair with them, and the matcha cannoli is the sweet finish.

Lee opened the restaurant earlier this year and says he asks customers for feedback to keep improving. He keeps the menu compact so his staff can do every dish well, and he buys ingredients from local sources so diners know where their food comes from.

Country Wok is at 107 Bangor Ave, Suite A, in downtown Hanceville. It is open Tuesday through Saturday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Order online at countrywok.com, through DoorDash, or by calling 256-887-1360.

headline: Sheriff's environmental deputy pulls up to 35 tons of trash a year off Cullman County roads
summary: Deputy Ron Wood and the sheriff's litter crew clean about 100 miles of county roads each year, and money from the recyclables they collect goes to local nonprofits.
body: If a county road near you looks cleaner than it used to, you may have Environmental Deputy Ron Wood to thank.
The Cullman County Sheriff's Office says Wood collects an estimated 50,000 to 70,000 pounds of roadside litter each year. That works out to about 25 to 35 tons from roughly 100 miles of roadway.

The program also gives back. Recyclable materials the crew picks up are sold, and the money is donated to nonprofits across Cullman County. In 2018, aluminum cans the crew collected brought in more than $1,300 for Cullman Caring for Kids.
The sheriff's office says the work has earned repeated recognition from Alabama People Against a Littered State, known as Alabama PALS, through its Governor's Awards law enforcement category.

Sheriff Matt Gentry praised Wood's dedication, saying the work keeps roads clean, protects the environment and helps local nonprofits. You can help too: secure truck loads and keep trash in the vehicle until you reach a can.

headline: County Commission pays for tornado siren repairs, adopts a five year hazard plan and thanks two departing members
summary: At its Oct. 20 meeting the Cullman County Commission approved about $39,000 in siren repairs, a new Hazard Mitigation Plan, a lower speed limit on County Road 52 and new cabins at Stony Lonesome OHV Park.
body: The Cullman County Commission handled a long list of business at its Tuesday, Oct. 20, meeting, and several items touch families all over the county, Hanceville included.

Storm safety led the way. Commissioners approved $39,293.11 to dB Telco for tornado siren repairs and adopted a five year Hazard Mitigation Plan for the county. A plan like this maps out the risks a county faces, such as tornadoes and flooding, and keeps the county in line for federal mitigation grants.
Drivers should note that the commission lowered the speed limit on County Road 52 to 25 mph. It also approved a paving agreement for County Road 102.

Stony Lonesome OHV Park in Bremen is getting new cabins. Adams Building Co. won the bids for accessible cabins and standard cabins, and Burks Building won the bid for metal storage buildings. The work is funded through a federal Recreational Trails Program grant. A bid for security fencing was rejected because it did not meet the bid requirements.

Other spending included a new roof for the Clarkson Covered Bridge cabin, 10 concrete pads at Smith Lake Park and payoffs on a Water Department excavator and two Road Department loaders. The commission also proclaimed October as Domestic Violence Awareness Month.

Chairman Jeff Clemons thanked Commissioners Kerry Watson of District 1 and Gary Marchman of District 2, who are leaving after 12 years each. Kenneth Walker will be sworn in for District 1 and Richard Barnett for District 2 in November.

The swearing in is set for 9 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 11, followed by the organizational meeting at 10. The next work session is Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 4 p.m., with the regular meeting at 6, at the Cullman County Courthouse. We added that meeting to our events page.

headline: Christmas plans, a storm prep tax holiday and hiring rules filled Hanceville's Oct. 22 council agenda
summary: The city posted the agenda for Thursday's council meeting. It lists the downtown trunk or treat, the Christmas parade and tree lighting, a severe weather sales tax holiday resolution and a plan to move the Thanksgiving Day meeting.
body: The City of Hanceville has posted the agenda for the council's Thursday, Oct. 22, meeting, and it gives a good look at what is coming up around town this fall and winter. The work session was set for 6 p.m. at City Hall, with the regular meeting right after.

Holiday plans take up a big part of the new business list. The council had the Downtown Trunk or Treat, the Tinsel Trail and Christmas Tree Lighting, and the Christmas Parade on the agenda. Dates for those events were not printed on the agenda, so we will add them to our events page as soon as the city or the organizers post them.

Also listed was Resolution 2026-1022 on the Severe Weather Preparedness Sales Tax Holiday. Alabama holds that holiday each February so families can stock up on things like flashlights, batteries and weather radios, and each city decides whether to drop its own sales tax for the weekend too.

Other new items included bill approval, reappointments to the Historic Preservation Commission, a tractor bid for Public Works and a plan to reschedule the Nov. 26 meeting, which falls on Thanksgiving Day.

Several items from the Oct. 8 meeting came back as old business. They include Councilman Robert Powell's take home vehicle policy, a citywide credit card policy, a formal interview process for city leadership jobs, and three ordinances on how the fire chief, public works director and park director are appointed.
Staff reports on bank balances, the fire department and Public Works and parks job details rounded out the night.

An agenda shows what the council planned to take up, not how members voted. We will share the results once the city posts minutes or video, or local reporters cover the meeting. The next regular meeting is Thursday, Nov. 12, at 6 p.m., and the new date for the second November meeting has not been announced yet.

headline: Register to vote by Monday, Oct. 19, and get to know the five amendments on the Nov. 3 ballot
summary: Monday is the last day to register for the Nov. 3 general election. Cullman County voters will also decide four statewide amendments and one local question about freezing property values for qualifying seniors.
body: If you want a say in the Nov. 3 general election, Monday, Oct. 19, is the day to circle. Alabama Secretary of State Wes Allen says that is the last day to register to vote. You can register online through the Secretary of State's website until 11:59 p.m. that night, mail a form postmarked by Monday, or turn one in to the Cullman County Board of Registrars before the office closes.

Other dates are close behind. The state voter guide lists Oct. 27 as the last day to apply for an absentee ballot by mail and Oct. 29 as the last day to apply in person. Absentee ballots returned by mail must arrive by noon on Election Day.

Below the races for office, every voter in Cullman County will see five yes or no questions. Statewide Amendment 1 combines three changes in one vote. It would let voters fill a lieutenant governor vacancy that happens early in a term, let the Legislature set pay for the lieutenant governor and legislative officers by joint resolution, and require a legislative officer to approve travel spending.

Statewide Amendment 2 would set up a process for neighboring county school systems to merge under one board, with a state impact study and a way for voters to protest. The Cullman Tribune notes it would not automatically combine Cullman City Schools and Cullman County Schools.

Statewide Amendment 3 would require local school boards to adopt policies for the Pledge of Allegiance at the start of each school day and to allow voluntary prayer that students start and lead. Statewide Amendment 4 would require public schools to play or perform the first verse of The Star Spangled Banner at least once a week.

The local question would let homeowners age 65 and older freeze the assessed value of their home for property taxes. The home must have been their main residence for at least five years, and there is no income limit. Claims could start Oct. 1, 2027, and a tax bill could still change if millage rates change.

You can read the official Fair Ballot Commission statement for each statewide amendment on the Secretary of State's website, and the Cullman County Probate Office posts a sample ballot before Election Day. Questions about the senior property freeze can go to the Revenue Commissioner's Office at 256-775-4776.

headline: Listerhill Credit Union opens its new Cullman branch and gives $10,000 to Cullman County Schools
summary: The credit union held a grand opening Thursday at 702 Industrial Dr. SW and handed Superintendent Dr. Shane Barnette a $10,000 check for the county school system.
body: Listerhill Credit Union celebrated its new Cullman branch with a grand opening on Thursday, Oct. 15, at 702 Industrial Dr. SW, The Cullman Tribune reported. The credit union broke ground on the site in November 2025 and moved in on Sept. 16.

During the ceremony, Listerhill presented a $10,000 check to Cullman County Schools, and Superintendent Dr. Shane Barnette accepted it for the school system. Cullman County Schools runs the public schools in Hanceville, from Hanceville Primary through Hanceville High. The Tribune's story did not say how the money will be used.

The opening fell on International Credit Union Day, which CEO Brad Green called a fitting way to celebrate. Board Chairman Mark Linder said Listerhill now has more than $1.5 billion in assets and about 92,000 members. It all started in 1952, when seven workers at the Reynolds Metals plant in Florence each put in $5 so their coworkers could borrow without turning to predatory lenders.

Cullman Mayor Woody Jacobs, Sheriff Matt Gentry, Sheriff-elect Chad Whaley and other local leaders were thanked at the event. For branch information, call Listerhill at 256-383-9204 or visit listerhill.com.

headline: Hanceville council adds $25,000 for road patching, backs mayor on fire chief
summary: More gas tax money is going toward potholes, a take home vehicle policy is still up for debate, and the council upheld the mayor's removal of the fire chief. The next meeting is Thursday, Oct. 22, at 6 p.m.
body: Potholes were near the top of the list when the Hanceville City Council met on Oct. 8. Council members approved another $25,000 from gas tax money so Public Works can keep patching streets, according to The Cullman Tribune.

The job has turned out bigger than planned. Rusty Fields of Public Works said the damaged spots vary a lot in size and depth, which takes extra time and material. City and county crews are working together at a cost of about $5,000 to $5,500 a day. Fields told the council they are a little more than halfway through.

Take home trucks took up the most time. Councilman Robert Powell has proposed a policy, Resolution 2026-8, that would limit everyday take home vehicles to department heads and employees who are on call. He pointed to fuel, insurance and upkeep, and one estimate put six take home vehicles at roughly $17,000 a year.

Public Works employees pushed back. They said having a truck at home gets them to downed trees, flooding and storm damage faster, and some keep their own tools in those trucks. The council added emergency exceptions and a six month phase out, then held the final vote for its next meeting.

The council also talked about having a say in hiring the fire chief, public works director and park director. Mayor Nolan Bradford said he wants to keep that authority with the mayor. No action was taken.

After about 40 minutes in executive session, the council voted unanimously to uphold Bradford's removal of Fire Chief Chris Hardin, who started in March. The Tribune reported that no reason was given in public and no replacement was named. The Cullman Times reported the vote as well.

A few other notes from the meeting: firefighters answered 116 calls in September, the city gave $500 to the North Alabama Agriplex, Councilman Cameron Rowe joined the Planning Commission, and work is moving ahead on policies needed to bring back a city police department.
If you want to speak up, the next council meeting is Thursday, Oct. 22, at 6 p.m.

summary: The weekend food program filled 3,800 bags for Hanceville students last school year and now takes donations through Cash App.
body: Hanceville Knapsacks for Kids sends students home with food for the weekend. The program filled 3,800 bags last school year, and it now accepts donations through Cash App, The Cullman Tribune reported.

headline: Meet your Hanceville City Council before the Nov. 12 meeting
summary: Hanceville's five council members and the Mayor meet next on Thursday, Nov. 12, at City Hall. Here is who represents you and how to follow along.
body: The Hanceville City Council meets next on Thursday, Nov. 12, at City Hall, 112 Main Street SE. A work session starts at 6:00 PM, and the regular meeting begins right after it.

The council has five members. Jana Shelton holds Place 1 and serves as Mayor Pro Tem. Robert Powell holds Place 2, Kim Brown holds Place 3, Cameron Rowe holds Place 4 and Carla Cain holds Place 5. Mayor Nolan Bradford also votes on council business. Each seat is elected to a four year term.
The council passes ordinances and resolutions, approves the yearly budget and keeps an eye on how city money and property are used. It also makes some appointments to city boards.

Every regular meeting is open to the public, and there is time set aside for public comments. If you can't make it, the city posts meeting videos on its YouTube channel. Draft agendas and minutes go up on the city's documents page, and they can change until the council approves them.
You can see photos of each council member, the full meeting schedule and links to agendas and minutes on our new City Council page.
